newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut prosecutor charges four over Netanyahu book.
newsitem.headline: Beirut prosecutor charges four over Netanyahu book.

text.p: A Lebanese prosecutor on Friday demanded up to 10 years in jail for four people charged with importing an Arabic version of a banned book written by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Prosecutor-general Abdullah Bitar charged three Lebanese -- a bookshop owner, a printing press owner and a shipping company owner -- and an unidentified Jordanian with importing the translation of Netanyahu's book 'A Place Among the Nations'.
The prosecutor said in an indictment that Netanyahu's book was banned because "it touches the national feeling, invokes racism and fanaticism and disturbs peace".
Lebanon and Israel are officially in a state of war despite five years of peace talks. Israeli troops occupy a strip of south Lebanon.
If convicted, the four charged could face between three and 10 years in jail, judicial sources said.

The independent Lebanese newspaper an-Nahar said on Friday police had confiscated 855 copies of Netanyahu's book from a printing company and a shipping company in Beirut. It said the book was translated into Arabic by a Jordanian.
English and Arabic versions of books written by Netayahu's moderate predecessor Shimon Peres are available in Beirut bookshops.
Netanyahu came to power in May on a platform opposing Arab-Israeli peace talks on the basis of exchanging occupied Arab land for peace.
